terms.meaning: A rule that forwards a web address to another place without the browser noticing.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Hosting and forwarding settings
sections.what: Sets the build command, the output folder, and the forwarding of /api calls to the hosted backend, plus a header that allows any site to read responses.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the live site call the backend through its own address.
sections.watch_out: The backend address is fixed in this file, so a backend move breaks the live site until this file is updated.

summary: Tells the hosting service how to build the frontend and forwards requests that start with /api to the hosted backend.
purpose: Sets up the live website on the hosting service.
why: Likely reason: the browser calls /api on the same site, so the host forwards those calls to the backend and avoids cross-site requests.
how: It sets the build command, the output folder, and the framework. It forwards any path under /api to the hosted backend, removing the /api prefix. It also adds a header to every route that allows any website to read the responses.
inputs: The repository, the build command, and the backend address written in the file.
outputs: The built website in the dist folder and forwarded API responses.
risks: The backend address is written into this file, so moving the backend means editing this file. The allow-any-site header applies to every route and is broader than needed.
debug: If API calls fail only on the live site, check the backend address here and whether that backend is running. If the deploy fails, check the build logs for errors from the build command.
